title: Calegari, scl, the graph-of-free-groups theorem in the free and surface groups chapter
body:
## The reference

Danny Calegari, *scl*, MSJ Memoirs volume 20, Mathematical Society of Japan, 2009.

Chapter: **Free and surface groups**. Section: **The Rationality Theorem**. Subsection:
**Injective, extremal, isometric maps**. The statement is the theorem labelled
`injective_surface_graph` in the source; its printed number is not recorded here, because
the build files in the source directory are empty and the number could not be recovered
from the manuscript. Somebody with a printed copy should supersede this record with it.

Part (3) of that theorem reads:

> Let G be a finite graph of free groups, amalgamated along cyclic subgroups. Let
> g_1, ..., g_n in G be conjugate into (free) vertex subgroups of G. Then scl is piecewise
> rational linear on the intersection of <g_1, ..., g_n> with B_1^H(G), and every rational
> chain in this subspace rationally bounds an extremal surface.

Only a sketch of the proof is given there. The details are in:

Danny Calegari, *Surface subgroups from homology*, Geometry & Topology **12** (2008),
1995-2007.

## Why it is relevant

This is what gives rationality for a chain in a closed hyperbolic surface group disjoint
from a simple essential curve. Cutting the surface along the curve presents its
fundamental group as a graph of free groups amalgamated over the cyclic subgroup carried
by the curve -- an amalgam if the curve separates, an HNN extension if not. A chain
disjoint from the curve is carried by the complementary pieces, so its terms are conjugate
into the free vertex subgroups, and part (3) applies directly.

Note that part (3) gives more than rationality: it also produces an extremal surface. So
in this special case the question of whether extremal surfaces exist has a positive
answer, which is worth knowing when considering the general question.
